Solar panels are impractical due to limited space on the remote, reducing space for the interface and for harvesting energy.
Adopt a combined power system using a rechargeable battery with kinetic energy as a back-up.
Charge the battery when the remote is moved.
The remote will use rubber casing material.
The casing must be firm and not bendable.
The touch-screen concept will be housed in a protective case to prevent breakage.
Parental control will be incorporated but not too complex and offered as a menu option.
The remote will use a square LCD as the standard touch-screen; if LCD is used, include an advanced LCD option.
Budget constraints may force moving from advanced chip sets to simpler button solutions if costs are not manageable.
